outcome: every inquiry arrives with the details the owner needs
label: Lead capture & qualification
problem: Inquiries arrive as vague one-line messages, so the owner plays phone tag before knowing if the job fits.
summary: A short, friendly request flow that asks the 3-5 questions the owner always asks, then shows a clean lead card.
steps: Owner reviews a scored lead card
features: Multi-step request form with progress bar
Lead card with priority tag (demo data)
Thank-you screen with honest response-time expectation
demoScope: Owner lead list with 6 synthetic leads

outcome: customers book themselves instead of waiting on a reply
label: Online booking & scheduling
problem: Booking happens by DM and phone, so slots go unfilled and the owner answers the same availability question all day.
summary: A booking flow with service picker, staff/time-slot selection and a confirmation screen, all on demo availability.
features: Service menu with duration and price range

outcome: customers see a ballpark before anyone drives out
label: Instant quote / estimate calculator
problem: Customers want a ballpark price before they call; the owner wastes trips quoting jobs that never book.
summary: An interactive estimator that turns a few inputs into a clearly-labeled price range using sample rates.
steps: See a ballpark range with assumptions
features: Price range built from labeled sample rates (not real pricing)
guard: Prices are illustrative sample rates; never present as the business's real pricing.

outcome: the cancellation policy is clear before the appointment
label: Deposits & checkout flow
problem: No-shows and last-minute cancellations cost real money because nothing is collected up front.
summary: A checkout and deposit flow mockup that shows policy, amount and receipt, with no live payment processing.
steps: Enter card on a mock form
features: Deposit step with clear policy text (mock)
Mock checkout form (no real payments processed)
guard: Payment UI is a mockup; it must state that no real payment is processed.

outcome: new clients arrive with their details already in
label: Onboarding & intake wizard
problem: New clients fill out paper forms or long PDFs, and key details get lost before the first visit.
summary: A step-by-step intake wizard that collects only demo fields and ends in a tidy profile summary.
guard: Intake collects synthetic fields only; no real personal, medical or financial data.

outcome: clients get a nudge and a one-tap way to reschedule
label: Reminders & no-show reduction
problem: Clients forget appointments and renewals, so the schedule has holes that nobody notices until too late.
summary: A reminder timeline that shows what message goes out when, with message previews and a confirm/reschedule flow.
features: Message previews (mock — no SMS or email is sent)
Unconfirmed list for the owner (demo data)
guard: Reminders are previews; never claim SMS/email is actually sent.

outcome: clients check status instead of calling
label: Customer portal & status tracking
problem: Clients call to ask 'where are we at?' because progress lives in the owner's head.
summary: A logged-in-style portal mockup with project timeline, documents, messages and next steps on demo data.
differentiators: Single source of truth for the client

outcome: regulars have a reason to come back sooner
label: Loyalty & rewards
problem: Regulars get the same treatment as first-timers, so there is no reason to come back sooner.
summary: A digital punch card / points wallet with a rewards catalog and a staff 'add visit' screen on demo data.

outcome: regulars can commit to a plan instead of one-off visits
label: Memberships, packages & subscriptions
problem: Revenue is lumpy because every visit is a one-off sale.
summary: A membership/package comparison page plus a member dashboard showing usage, renewal date and perks.
steps: Member dashboard shows usage and renewal
guard: Membership checkout is a mockup; no recurring billing is set up.

outcome: shoppers see what's in stock before they visit
label: Inventory & stock visibility
problem: Customers call to ask if something is in stock, and staff check the back room every time.
summary: A product catalog with live-looking stock badges, low-stock alerts and a simple restock view on demo data.

outcome: the owner sees the week on one screen
label: Owner dashboard & reporting
problem: The owner runs the business from memory and a notes app, with no single view of the week.
summary: A one-screen owner dashboard with clearly-labeled sample KPIs, a jobs/appointments table and filters.
guard: All numbers are synthetic sample data, labeled as such; never present as real business results.

outcome: crews get a clear day plan instead of a text thread
label: Scheduling, dispatch & routes
problem: Crews zig-zag across town because jobs are assigned by text message.
summary: A dispatch board with drag-to-assign jobs, crew lanes and a route-order preview on demo data.
features: Route-order preview (static demo, no live maps)
guard: Route view is a static illustration; never claim live GPS or maps integration.

outcome: happy customers get an easy path to share feedback
label: Reviews & reputation requests
problem: Happy customers never leave reviews, so the listing doesn't reflect the real work.
summary: A post-visit feedback flow that routes happy customers to a review step and captures private feedback.
steps: Unhappy path: private feedback to owner
guard: Never fabricate reviews or ratings; sample feedback is clearly labeled synthetic.

outcome: word of mouth gets tracked and thanked
label: Referral program
problem: Word of mouth is the best channel but nobody tracks or thanks referrers.
summary: A referral page with shareable code, referral tracker and a thank-you reward flow on demo data.

outcome: orders arrive complete instead of scribbled on a ticket
label: Online ordering & preorders
problem: Orders come in by phone at peak time and get written on tickets, so mistakes and lost orders happen.
summary: A menu/catalog ordering flow with modifiers, pickup time slots and an order-status screen on demo data.
features: Menu with modifiers and dietary tags
guard: Checkout is a mockup; no payment processing or POS integration.

outcome: people hold a spot instead of walking away
label: Waitlist & capacity
problem: When it's full, people walk away or call repeatedly instead of holding a spot.
summary: A join-the-waitlist flow with live-looking position, estimated wait and owner capacity view on demo data.

outcome: prospects can actually see the quality of the work
label: Interactive gallery & before/after
problem: The work is great but it's buried in a camera roll, so prospects can't see the quality.
summary: A filterable portfolio with before/after sliders and a 'get this look' inquiry, using placeholder imagery.
guard: Use placeholder or licensed stock imagery; never present stock photos as the business's real work.

outcome: families see the day without texting staff
label: Family & caregiver updates feed
problem: Families text all day asking how things are going, and staff can't answer while working.
summary: A daily updates feed with activity cards, simple icons and an end-of-day summary, using fictional placeholder profiles.
guard: Fictional placeholder profiles only; no real names or photos of children, seniors or clients.

outcome: customers stay on a schedule instead of calling only in emergencies
label: Recurring service & maintenance plans
problem: Customers only call when something breaks, so work is reactive and seasonal.
summary: A maintenance-plan page with tiers, a service calendar and a member view of upcoming visits.

outcome: spots are tracked in one place instead of DMs
label: Class & event registration
problem: Spots for classes and events are tracked in DMs and spreadsheets, so overbooking and no-shows happen.
summary: A schedule with class cards, capacity bars, registration and a check-in list on demo data.

outcome: the same ten questions get answered without the owner
label: FAQ assistant concept (scripted)
problem: The same ten questions eat the owner's evenings (hours, prices, availability, what to bring).
summary: A chat-style assistant concept with scripted answers from a visible FAQ list and a human-handoff button.
steps: Assistant answers from the FAQ list
Unknown → hands off to a human form
features: Chat widget with scripted replies (concept — not a live AI)
guard: Scripted concept only; never claim a working AI receptionist or that it answers calls.

outcome: customers see progress and approve work in one tap
label: Job status & approvals
problem: Customers drop something off and hear nothing until they call; approvals for extra work stall jobs.
summary: A job tracker with stage timeline, photo-backed findings and an approve/decline step on demo data.

outcome: supporters can give or sign up in a minute
label: Donations & volunteer signup
problem: Supporters want to help but the 'how' is a PDF and an email address.
summary: A give/volunteer hub with impact stories (placeholder), shift signup and a mock donation flow.
guard: Impact numbers and stories are placeholders; never invent real outcomes.

outcome: people can browse and inquire without a phone call
label: Listings search & inquiry
problem: Inventory (units, homes, vehicles, roles) lives in a spreadsheet, so browsing and inquiring is painful.
summary: A filterable listings grid with detail pages, saved favorites and an inquiry/tour request on demo data.
